Heavy drinking always carries risks.  But increasingly, studies 
are showing that light drinking (defined as 1 drink or less a
day for women and 2 drinks or less a day for men) may have
some health benefits.
Perhaps the most significant benefit is in cardiovascular
health.  Alcohol may help increase levels of high-density
lipoprotein (“good”) cholesterol and may help reduce the
clotting that can lead to a heart attack or stroke.  Red wine
also is thought to contain phytochemicals (compounds
occurring in plants) that also may help protect against
cardiovascular disease.
